title: Use a dot for lateral variation in artifact names

facts.note: Planner role/phase is not currently emitted as an observable fact; needs a phase observer.
Task text mentions naming artifacts or variants. Illustrative trigger only; the rule applies wherever an artifact name is authored.
Diff-level detection of a new or renamed artifact name requires an artifact-name observer, independent of the file it appears in.
Whether a name expresses a lateral variant (same conceptual level, different flavor/state/type/facet) vs. a deeper/different level needs semantic judgment.

fires: A planner names an artifact that is a particular flavor, state, type or facet of an aspect, even if it is the only variant named so far.
A planner names artifacts for distinct states of one aspect (e.g. an active vs. a closed state).
A planner renames an artifact variant that currently uses a non-dot separator for a lateral difference.
doesNotFire: The name expresses a different, deeper or hierarchical level rather than a lateral variant of an aspect (separator choice is governed by separator semantics).
Work that does not author or rename any artifact name.

given: A planner is authoring or renaming an artifact name.
when: The name expresses a lateral variation: the same conceptual level as its aspect, differing in flavor, state, type or facet.
then: Mark the lateral variation with a dot: append the variant to the aspect name after a dot (aspect.variant).
prefer: Follow the illustrative pattern domain:aspect.variant, e.g. domain:aspect.variantA vs domain:aspect.variantB for two states of one aspect.
Use the dot suffix for a different flavor, state, type or facet of the same aspect.
avoid: Using a dot for something that is not at the same conceptual level (a deeper or different aspect).
Encoding a lateral variant with another separator or by inventing a new aspect name, which hides that the artifacts are variants of one aspect.
why: A dot signals that artifacts are variants of one aspect, so readers and tooling can tell flavor/state variants apart from different aspects or levels.
evidence: Each artifact name that expresses a flavor/state/type/facet of an aspect carries that variant after a dot.
Reviewer confirms dot-suffixed names really are lateral (same conceptual level), consistent with the separator semantics convention.
verifier_detail: Canonical source examples of compliant lateral variants: 'sensory:gesture.raw vs sensory:gesture.tapped'; 'player:session.active vs player:session.closed'; 'match:config.duel vs match:config.team'.
Term lateral_variation: a different flavor/state of the same aspect, marked by a dot.
Lateral = same conceptual level; variant kinds covered: flavor, state, type, facet. Applies to a single variant name; no existing sibling is required.
